canonical_statement: The network meta-analysis aimed to compare glucose-lowering drug classes for glucose control, body weight, hypoglycemia, gastrointestinal adverse events, and quality of life.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Aim of the present network meta-analysis is the comparison across glucose-lowering drugs concerning their effects on glucose control, body weight, hypoglycemia, gastrointestinal adverse events, and quality of life.

canonical_statement: Eligible studies were randomized controlled trials comparing different glucose-lowering agents against other active drugs with duration of at least 52 weeks.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The present analysis includes all RCTs comparing different GLA versus other active drugs, with a duration ≥ of 52 weeks.

population.label: Randomized active-comparator trials in type 2 diabetes

canonical_statement: Placebo-controlled trials were excluded because the analysis was restricted to direct comparisons between active treatments.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The present analysis was restricted to direct comparisons between active treatments, with the exclusion of placebo-controlled trials.

population.label: Randomized active-comparator trials in type 2 diabetes

canonical_statement: Trials in which the protocol recommended adjustment of concurrent treatment to optimize glucose control, including then-available cardiovascular outcome trials, were excluded.

canonical_statement: The review was reported according to PRISMA and was registered in PROSPERO with provisional number 167026, uploaded January 5, 2020.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: This meta-analysis is reported following the criteria of Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) statement ... uploaded on PROSPERO on Jan 5th, 2020 ... provisional number #167026.

canonical_statement: Medline, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through January 1, 2020; reference lists were manually searched, and BASE and Open Grey were searched for grey literature.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A Medline, Embase, and Cochrane Library search, up to Jan 1st, 2020 ... References of retrieved articles were manually searched ... Bielefeld Academic Search Engine ... and Open Grey.

canonical_statement: Study searches and selection were independently performed by two authors, with conflicts resolved by a third investigator.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: These searches and the selection of studies were independently performed by two authors (M.M and L.N.) and conflicts resolved by a third investigator (E.M.).

canonical_statement: Data were extracted preferentially from the principal publication, with secondary publications and ClinicalTrials.gov used when needed; two authors extracted independently and a third resolved conflicts.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Summary estimates ... were extracted from the principal publication ... secondary publications and clinicaltrials.gov registry were used ... Data extraction was performed independently by two ... and conflicts resolved by a third investigator.

canonical_statement: Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane RCT risk-of-bias tool across seven domains and categorized as low, high, or uncertain risk.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The risk of bias was assessed using the Cochrane risk of bias tool for RCTs ... seven specific domains ... graded as low risk of bias, high risk of bias, or uncertain risk of bias.

canonical_statement: The principal outcome was HbA1c at 12, 52, and at least 104 weeks.

canonical_statement: Continuous outcomes were analyzed with a standardized/weighted mean-difference metric and categorical outcomes with Mantel-Haenszel odds ratios, using random-effects models and 95% confidence intervals.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: For each available comparison, the standardized difference in means (MD) for continuous variables, and Mantel-Haenszel Odds Ratio (MHeOR) for categorial variables were calculated, both with 95% Confidence Interval (CI), using random effect models.

canonical_statement: Statistical heterogeneity was assessed with I² and Cochran Q, and 52-week HbA1c funnel plots were used for direct comparisons with at least 10 studies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Statistical heterogeneity was assessed by the I2 test and Cochran’s Q test, whereas Funnel plots (for all direct comparisons with at least 10 studies) for HbA1c at 52 weeks were used to detect publication bias.

canonical_statement: The network meta-analysis used generalized pairwise modelling, with metformin as the overall reference; add-on-to-metformin sensitivity analysis used sulfonylureas as reference.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: We performed NMA within pairwise modelling (GPM) framework ... using metformin as reference ... in this latter analysis the reference category chosen was sulfonylureas.

canonical_statement: Network consistency was assessed with H values, with H below 3 defined by the authors as minimal inconsistency.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: To test consistency between direct and indirect evidence, H values were calculated; H < 3 indicates minimal inconsistency of treatment effects.

canonical_statement: Analyses were performed using Review Manager version 5.3 and MetaXL.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Analyses were performed using Review Manager (RevMan), Version 5.3 ... and MetaXL.
